name: engine-ext-v1
about: The in-process extension interface of a TandemLLM engine (ENG-429). Python, not HTTP. The engine owns it; TandemApp's conductor is its first extension. README.md says it in prose; fake_host.py is the reference host and fake_ext.py the smallest extension. A minor step adds a hook, an argument with a default, a host attribute, an event field or an act kind; a major step removes or renames one or changes a meaning.

discovery.headless: QSE_EXT empty or unset: no extension; the engine serves its own routes only

module.EXT_API: the interface version the extension was written against, 'MAJOR.MINOR'
module.NAME: a short name, shown in /health extensions

discovery.accepts: the same MAJOR as the host and a MINOR at or below the host's

host.state: the server's state mapping (read; the extension writes only keys it owns)
host.lock: the engine lock; a hook never holds it across a call back into the host
host.metrics: the metrics registry handle: add(family) for the families metrics-families.json lists with owner ext; since 1.3 event(row): one journal row of the extension (its decisions) counted in those families
host.ledger_path: the ledger file; the extension owns its own tables in it (conductor_events, its version row)
host.args: the parsed command line as a mapping, and QSE_EXT_ARGS (a JSON object, since 1.1) over it: its keys win
host.engine: the engine-only screens in process: residency_plan, disk, disk_clear, deciders, narrator, shadow (the /v1/engine/* handlers)
host.log: log(line): one line into the engine's log
host.Refusal: the exception plan raises to answer the client with an error: Refusal(status, type, message), since 1.2 with a fourth argument param (the request field it names, in the error's param)
host.ext_dir: since 1.3: the directory the engine was given for the extension's own documents (--conductor-config), or None (the extension runs without one: chat mode always has one)
host.identity_name: since 1.3: identity_name() -> str or None, the served model's identity name (the weight profile's), for the extension's answers
host.own_eta: since 1.3: own_eta(texts, max_new) -> milliseconds or None, how long the engine's own model would take to answer a question of the extension now; the attribute is None when the engine keeps no estimate (QWEN38_OWN_ETA off)
host.own_idle: since 1.3: own_idle() -> seconds or None, how long no client request has been decoding (None: one is decoding now)
host.NoRoom: since 1.3: the exception the engine's callbacks raise inside in_context, ask_in_place and settle_claim when the window has no room for the question (its why: no_room)

attributes.routes: [{method, prefix, handler}]: paths the extension serves (method * for any; a prefix ending in / matches below it, any other the path itself and below it); handler(request) -> (status, headers, body), request with method, path, query, headers, body, peer and auth (since 1.1), and since 1.3 allowed(route) (None, or the engine's refusal (status, headers, body) for that access rule), session_token and session (the session address /s/<token> the path came under and the session key it names, else None). A prefix the engine serves itself is refused at start
attributes.models: [model entry]: what /v1/models lists in place of the engine's own model (the TandemLLM alias); since 1.1 read at every /v1/models answer, so it may follow the extension's own documents, and /v1/models/{id} answers an entry of that id, or the first entry for the engine's own model name (a hidden alias)

hooks.name: health
hooks.when: each full /health answer: merged under loaded

hooks.name: plan
hooks.when: before the request queues, without the engine lock; None serves the request as a headless engine would

hooks.name: prompt
hooks.when: the prompt's token ids before prefill (the router's notes replayed); since 1.2 info {in_think, conv} says whether the prompt ends inside <think> and names the conversation, and an extension on 1.2 may answer the ids with in_think (it closed the block) and client_ids (the prompt as the client sent it, None when it put nothing in); a host asks an extension before 1.2 with plan and ids only

hooks.name: supervisor
hooks.when: once the prompt is built: the object the decode loop asks at the safe points

hooks.name: extras
hooks.when: point start, block or finish: items {kind, data} the engine puts into the stream (state lines, narrated lines); start may come before prompt and supervisor (the lines a request shows while it waits)

hooks.name: follow_ups
hooks.when: the turn's end: own-work requests {kind, what, body} the engine schedules after the client's

hooks.name: finish
hooks.when: the request's ledger row is written: the extension writes its journal rows

extension.calls_about: since 1.3: optional methods of the extension object the request path asks, each open like a hook (a raise or a missing method: the headless value; a raise is counted under the call's name). An extension before 1.3 is not asked them. routing is the plan's routing object

calls.name: server_mode
calls.when: before plan: the extension's mode for the request (raw, shadow or on), lowered by the client's X-Tandem header (header), never above shadow for n > 1 choices; the engine names it in the X-Tandem answer header

calls.name: served_name
calls.when: the model name the engine answers under while the extension routes requests (TandemLLM); None: the engine's own

calls.name: side_first_max
calls.when: a side request (routing.side) whose prompt has at most this many tokens goes first

calls.name: strip_states
calls.when: a chat request routed by the extension: the client's messages without the state lines an earlier stream showed, and how many were taken out

calls.name: loop_escape
calls.when: a chat turn: info {body, session}; the profile's sampling section (agentic_default: card or None), the loop escape's step for the session (state: a mapping with state on or off, or None) and sampling(fallback) -> the card's sampling; the engine builds the sampler

calls.name: code_class
calls.when: the turn's class is a code class (the client's no-repeat n-gram mask is dropped on it)

calls.name: served
calls.when: the admission's dry run: the prompt as the extension would serve it, the plan left unchanged

calls.name: in_context
calls.when: the in-context stage, under the engine lock before the turn's prefill: the extension decides the turn's class over the prompt; choice(ids, letters, at) and rows(ids) are the engine's callbacks that read in the same slot, and raise the host's NoRoom when the window has no room

calls.name: settle_context
calls.when: the in-context stage cannot run (why: prompt_too_long): the extension decides without it

calls.name: ask_in_place
calls.when: routing.ask is set: the extension's pending question asked in place over the prompt (choice as for in_context); the engine sets routing.ask to None after it

calls.name: route_lines
calls.when: once the plan is applied: the plan's own state lines into the lines object's ui

calls.name: memory_filter
calls.when: a streamed chat answer: the filter that keeps the extension's memory blocks on the server: feed(text) -> text for each content piece outside the reasoning, finish() -> text at the end, and its fields hidden (the blocks kept) and failed, which the engine journals; None: no filter

calls.name: memory_spans
calls.when: after the answer: where the memory blocks taken out of it (taken, their texts) sit in ids (decode(ids) -> text): [[start, end]], and how many were not found

calls.name: answer_mask
calls.when: a chat request: the secret echo mask over the answer: push(text, field) -> text, held(field) -> bool, finish(field) -> text while streaming, text(text, field) -> text for a whole answer, and its fields counts (a mapping) and replace (masked, else shadow)

calls.name: replayed
calls.when: a cache peek in chat mode: the prompt's ids with the extension's notes for the session replayed into them, as the prefill will see them

calls.name: turn_ended
calls.when: the turn's answer went out: the supervisor's idle time starts (its watch)

calls.name: writer_ban_ids
calls.when: the memory writer's own turn: the logit biases that keep it from opening another tool's call

calls.name: writer_foreign_call
calls.when: the memory writer's own turn: where its answer turns into a call of another tool (the engine cuts there), or None

calls.name: probe_stage
calls.when: a request with a probe capture: the router's probe stage settings ({mode, ...}; mode off or None: no stage)

plan_fields.active: bool: the plan changes the request; false hands every step its input back
plan_fields.body: dict or None: the body the engine serves in place of the client's
plan_fields.routing: since 1.3: the extension's routing of the request, or None (a plan that only supervises: the monitor alone). The engine reads and writes the fields routing_fields names and hands it to the calls

routing_fields.active: bool: the routing changes the request (as plan.active)
routing_fields.row: mapping: the extension's journal row of the request; the engine reads id, class_id, effort, source, injected, replayed and acted, and writes its own facts under row['extra'] (a mapping), which finish journals
routing_fields.side: mapping or None: a side request (the extension's own question, a client's side request); the engine reads max_tokens and writes first (bool: served first)
routing_fields.session: object or None: the session the extension keeps for the conversation; key (str) and notes (list)
routing_fields.res: object: the request's profile, resolved: mode (raw, off, shadow or on), profile (its name), doc (the profile document, a mapping; the engine reads its shadow section)
routing_fields.headers: headers() -> [[name, value]]: the answer headers the extension adds
routing_fields.think_budget: think_budget(budget) -> int: the reasoning budget the route gives for the server's budget
routing_fields.decides_effort: bool: the route decides the reasoning effort (a client's effort word is read through think_budget)
routing_fields.client_word: str: what the route does with a client's effort word (ignore, ...)
routing_fields.budget: truthy when the route set a reasoning budget (the supervisor closes the reasoning there)
routing_fields.thinking_off: bool: the route turned thinking off
routing_fields.transcript: str: full keeps the turn's transcript
routing_fields.context: object or None: the in-context stage is due (in_context)
routing_fields.ask: object or None: a question asked in place is due (ask_in_place); the engine sets it to None once asked
routing_fields.compaction: bool: the turn is a compaction
routing_fields.compaction_ids: list[int] or None: the engine writes the compaction's summary ids here
routing_fields.changed: bool: prompt put something into the ids
routing_fields.prompt_client: bool: the prompt is served as the client rendered it
routing_fields.block: mapping or None: this turn's notes block (items: their texts)
routing_fields.injected: list or None: the packages put into the prompt ({parts})
routing_fields.spans: list: the notes' hidden spans in the prompt
routing_fields.head_ids: list[int] or None: the prompt's head as the extension renders it
routing_fields.head_end: int or None: where that head ends
routing_fields.router_cfg: mapping or None: the router's settings (injection.max_note_tokens; probe_stage reads it)
routing_fields.probe_row: probe_row(prompt, tokenizer) -> mapping: the probe capture's row
routing_fields.memory: mapping or None: the request's memory settings (mode, text); the engine writes the memory facts under row['extra']['memory']

kinds.lines: since 1.3: data is the request's lines object (extras start), with the fields lines_fields names; the engine writes the state lines with it

lines_fields.ui: the lines' state object: add(...), log(...), take_kinds(...), pending, shown, head, states, voice, narrator; monitor(event), the supervisor's on_event
lines_fields.channel: str: where the lines go (the content, a status field)
lines_fields.progress: mapping: the prefill's progress line settings
lines_fields.MEMORY_KINDS: the kinds of the memory's lines
lines_fields.status_clients: the client kinds that get a status bar
lines_fields.inline: inline(line) -> text: a line as content
lines_fields.into_full: into_full(...) -> the lines into a whole (non-streamed) answer
lines_fields.share: share() -> the narrator's share of the decode

methods.name: check_answer
methods.about: SP3 for an answer's held calls at once (items: the calls, and the blocks that do not parse, as the answer has them); final: the answer ended without its end token. A supervisor without it (an extension before 1.2) is not asked

optional_methods.name: apply_request
optional_methods.about: SP4's acts spliced into the prompt (PROMPT_TAIL_NOTE at the tail)

optional_methods.name: route_budget
optional_methods.about: the request's reasoning cap (task: route, client or reserve) handed to the supervisor: true when it closes the reasoning there at SP1 (SET_THINK_BUDGET)

optional_methods.name: settle_claim
optional_methods.about: SP2's claim check asked in place: asker(question) answers in the same slot; the host's NoRoom ends it

optional_methods.name: without_notes
optional_methods.about: the answer as the client gets it: without the memory notes, and how many notes and note calls were taken out

optional_methods.name: as_sent
optional_methods.about: the held calls as they go out after the checks

optional_methods.name: release_call
optional_methods.headless: the call without its keys that start with _
optional_methods.about: a held call released to the client

optional_methods.name: release_block
optional_methods.about: a held block that does not parse released

optional_methods.name: note_repairs
optional_methods.about: the engine's repairs of a call's argument keys, for the journal

optional_methods.name: argloop_stopped
optional_methods.about: the argument loop guard stopped a call of the tool name (verdict), for the journal

policy.about: read: the policy's version (policy.version) for the usage frame

holds_calls.about: read: tool calls are held until SP3 has seen them

watches_blocks.about: read: SP1 is asked after each block

arms.about: read: the reasoning-loop detector's arms SP1 needs

acts.about: read: acts carried out that count against the caps

acted.about: read: an act changed the output

gave_up.about: read: the GIVE_UP sentence, once given up

final_answer.about: read: the answer sent in place of a generation (a give-up at SP4)

cuts.about: read: tokens sent before each regeneration began

forwarding.about: read: a hidden forward is running

forwarded_at.about: read: when the last hidden forward ended

memory_notes.about: read: what the memory filter takes out of the answer (SP2 reads past it)

on_event.about: read: the lines' hook for each decision

checked.about: read and written by the engine: SP3 ran over the answer that is ending

can_ask.about: written by the engine: the loop can ask a question in place now

lift_ids.about: written by the engine before at_finish: the calls' ids the output ended with inside its reasoning

held_events.about: written by the engine: SP2's events held while a block's tokens still go out

resume_ms.about: appended by the engine: SP2's end token to the continued answer's first token

act.executed_by: the engine, in the decode loop; ids are forwarded, visible (a suffix of ids) reaches the client
act.shape: a mapping with those keys, or (since 1.2) an object with them as attributes

since_1_2.events: request adds prompt_ids (the prompt as it will be prefilled so far), conv (the conversation's id, or null), chat (a chat request), tool_names (the offered tools the answer is read for), thinking_off (the client turned thinking off) and loop_escape (the loop escape's step for SP4's note, or null); events are mappings whose fields read as attributes too
since_1_2.SP2: at_finish may answer REGENERATE_CALL: an answer that ends on its end token with calls is checked there (SP3 asked at SP2), where the calls can still be written again
since_1_2.pass_through: an exception of the engine's own that an engine callback raises inside a hook (the client left: ConnectionError) is no failure of the extension: it goes on to the engine
since_1_2.interim: 1.2 only (ENG-413 WP3b): what the engine's request path asked an interim adapter outside this interface. 1.3 makes it the interface (since_1_3), except what kept_interim lists

since_1_3.host: ext_dir, identity_name, own_eta, own_idle and metrics.event: what an extension read of the engine outside the interface until 1.2
since_1_3.calls: extension.calls: the request path's optional calls, each with its headless value
since_1_3.routing: request.plan_fields.routing and request.routing_fields: what the engine reads and writes of the extension's routing
since_1_3.lines: extras.kinds.lines and extras.lines_fields: the lines object extras start answers
since_1_3.supervisor: supervisor.optional_methods (each with its headless value) and supervisor.fields (each with the value a supervisor that keeps none answers): what the decode loop asks and reads beyond the safe points' methods
since_1_3.routes: a route's request gains allowed(route) -> None or the engine's refusal (status, headers, body), session_token and session (the session address /s/<token> the path came under, and the session key it names, or None)
since_1_3.NoRoom: host.NoRoom: what the engine's callbacks raise when a question asked in place has no room in the window

kept_interim.where: server/ext.py INTERIM, asked like a call, counted as interim.writer
kept_interim.why: it hands the engine the extension's memory object, whose writer turn the engine drives itself (gate(router, conv), instructions, due, apply, mark, skipped, state, stats): freezing those as fields would make the writer's internals the interface. The right form is an own-work request the extension runs through a host callable that decodes a hidden turn; that is a new shape, not a field

kept_interim.what: the extension's objects in host.state the engine reads outside a request: state['conductor'] (store, router, library, root, the residency and shadow documents), state['monitor'].policy, state['conductor_policy'] (written by the engine before the load)
kept_interim.where: server/app.py: the shadow reader's preload, the library text, the decider claim, the residency journal, --backends, the policy check before the load
kept_interim.why: these are the engine-only screens and startup reads WP5 turns into /v1/engine/* and host callables; state['conductor'] is not None stays the engine's sign that the extension routes requests (chat mode), state['journal'] the extension's journal the engine closes at the drain

act_loops.CONTINUE_HIDDEN: at_finish -> the engine forwards ids and decodes on -> at_block* -> at_finish again
act_loops.REGENERATE_CALL: at_tool_call -> the engine cuts the call and decodes again from its start -> at_tool_call again
act_loops.GIVE_UP: the engine writes the visible text and ends the turn: at_finish is not asked again

failure.rule: closed at start, open per request
failure.start: QSE_EXT names a module that does not import, has no EXT_API or one the host does not accept, lacks a hook, raises in start, or claims an engine path; or chat mode is asked with QSE_EXT empty: the engine does not start and prints one line '[ext] REFUSING: <why>'. The module's checks (it imports, its attributes, EXT_API, chat without QSE_EXT, QSE_EXT_ARGS) refuse before the weights load; start(host) runs once the served model is loaded, since the host hands it the tokenizer and the engine, and a start that raises, a missing hook or a claimed path refuse before the engine takes its first request (since 1.1 said so). It never falls back to headless when an extension was asked for
failure.request: a hook that raises or returns a value of the wrong shape: the engine logs it, counts it (qse_ext_errors_total{hook}: the hook's or the supervisor method's name; models, route and stop too) and serves the rest of that request as a headless engine would: plan -> raw, prompt -> the ids as built, supervisor -> none from then on, extras -> none, follow_ups and finish -> skipped. Acts already carried out stay; the next request asks the extension again
failure.refusal: plan may raise the host's Refusal(status, type, message): the client gets that error; it is an answer, not a failure
failure.act_out_of_place: an act whose kind the safe point does not allow is dropped and counted, as an error of that hook
failure.route: a handler of the extension's own route that raises: 500 extension_error for that request, counted as hook route; there is no headless answer for a path only the extension serves
